executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated two separate epidemiological updates from PAHO (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating sustained zoonotic transmission pressure in the Americas region. Additional threats of concern include mpox, yellow fever, dengue, measles, and pertussis, with the Southern Hemisphere influenza season commencing in late April 2026 adding respiratory disease burden. The breadth and frequency of PAHO alerts suggest an unusually active multi-pathogen transmission period across the Western Hemisphere.
bottomLine: Sustained H5N1 activity in the Americas combined with simultaneous circulation of mpox, dengue, yellow fever, measles, and the onset of Southern Hemisphere influenza season signals a high-complexity, multi-threat epidemiological period requiring coordinated surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued within ~4 months (November 2025 and March 2026) indicating ongoing zoonotic activity
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential; continued animal-to-human spillover risk in the Americas
Sustained surveillance pressure prompting repeated regional alerts from PAHO
threats.action: Activate enhanced One Health surveillance protocols; increase genomic sequencing of H5N1 isolates; monitor healthcare workers and exposed agricultural populations; coordinate with FAO and OIE on animal reservoir control

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active transmission in the Americas
Ongoing global clade concerns following 2022-2024 outbreaks; potential for clade Ib introduction
Requires sustained community surveillance and vaccination campaign monitoring
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and case isolation; promote vaccination of high-risk populations; enhance genomic surveillance to detect clade variants; coordinate cross-border reporting

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating epizootic or human case activity
Sylvatic yellow fever risk in unvaccinated populations in endemic zones
Alert timing suggests early-season epizootics in South American jungle regions
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations; investigate epizootic activity in non-human primates as sentinel events; enforce traveler vaccination requirements for endemic zones

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 18 2026 following record 2024 outbreak year
Hyperendemicity with all four serotypes circulating increases severe dengue risk
Early 2026 alert suggests above-baseline transmission continuing into new season
threats.action: Intensify vector control (Aedes aegypti) programs; expand clinical surveillance for severe dengue; promote community education on larval source reduction; monitor serotype shifts

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / Southern Hemisphere Season Onset
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert April 27 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Simultaneous RSV co-circulation alert issued January 9 2026 indicating complex respiratory season
ECDC weekly threat reports covering Weeks 16-20 (April-May 2026) likely tracking Northern Hemisphere season transition
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination campaigns in Southern Hemisphere countries; strengthen hospital surge capacity for respiratory illness; monitor for novel reassortant strains given concurrent H5N1 activity

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO alerts issued (December 2025 and March 2026) indicating sustained or resurging transmission
Resurgence pattern consistent with global pertussis upswing reported in multiple regions in 2024-2026
Infants and unvaccinated individuals at highest risk of severe outcomes
threats.action: Review vaccination coverage rates especially in infants and pregnant women; implement targeted booster campaigns; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity for Bordetella pertussis

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026 indicating importation or outbreak risk
Vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic create susceptible cohorts
Americas region had achieved elimination status; any reintroduction requires urgent response
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments; implement outbreak response immunization in affected areas; strengthen airport and border point surveillance for imported cases

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika in Aedes-endemic zones complicates clinical differentiation
Potential for spread to previously unaffected areas via Aedes albopictus expansion
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance to differentiate chikungunya from dengue; strengthen vector control in affected municipalities; monitor for geographic spread into temperate Aedes albopictus zones

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent and has been flagged as a Critical threat based on two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 24 2025 and March 11 2026) documenting sustained activity in the Americas region. H5N1 carries significant pandemic potential due to its high case fatality rate in humans and ongoing zoonotic spillover from avian and mammalian reservoirs. No BSL-4 select agents were explicitly identified in the provided report titles; however, the ECDC weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20) may contain additional select agent signals not visible in the titles alone. Continued vigilance for BSL-4 agents (e.g., viral hemorrhagic fevers) is warranted given the active yellow fever alerts in the region.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific alerts identified in report titles; however Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given two pertussis alerts within 3 months
Sustained bacterial co-infections during influenza outbreaks may drive empirical antibiotic overuse; secondary bacterial pneumonia AMR surveillance recommended
Regional dengue management practices may involve antibiotic misuse for febrile illness misdiagnosis, contributing to AMR pressure in endemic zones
emergingPatterns: Dual H5N1 epidemiological updates within 4 months suggest accelerating zoonotic spillover pressure in the Americas, raising pandemic preparedness concern
Simultaneous circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) during early 2026 indicates unusually high Aedes-borne disease burden
Two pertussis alerts within 3 months (December 2025 and March 2026) suggest a resurgence wave consistent with waning immunity and post-pandemic vaccination gaps
Onset of Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with active H5N1 zoonotic activity creates conditions for potential reassortment events
PAHO alert on GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse (February 2026) signals emerging non-infectious public health threat intersecting with healthcare system capacity
ECDC issuing 5 consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) during a period of multiple concurrent alerts suggests elevated European surveillance posture
Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome alert (December 2025) combined with arboviral alerts suggests rodent reservoir activity may be elevated, potentially linked to ecological disruptions
Measles re-emergence alert in a region with prior elimination status reflects population immunity gaps requiring urgent catch-up vaccination campaigns
